title: GitHub Trending Summary - Daily - 2026-11-09
ranking_explanation: All 11 repositories on the captured daily Trending view are ranked by the displayed stars-today value in descending order. Current repository identities, default branches, and default-branch commit SHAs were corroborated with GitHub REST endpoints. Total star counts in this report are the values displayed on the captured Trending page.
global_caveat: GitHub Trending is a point-in-time attention signal, not a measure of project quality, usage, or why stars were gained. Daily gain and total-star counts can change. A GitHub Search scan of recently created and pushed repositories surfaced noisy or weakly substantiated hits; those were not promoted over repositories on the Trending page.

sections.title: Snapshot
sections.content: Daily snapshot at 2026-11-09 17:43 UTC; date range 2026-11-09 through 2026-11-09. Ranking basis: daily GitHub Trending star gains, corroborated against GitHub REST repository and commit data.

sections.title: Headline
sections.content: Sherlock leads today's star-gain list, while agent-building tools, an agent-ready design system, and an AI browser CLI form the strongest connected cluster. The rest of the page is notably mixed: open-source security search, physics simulation, Wi-Fi sensing, market analysis, and smart-home automation all draw attention alongside agent tooling.

sections.title: sherlock-project/sherlock
sections.description: Hunt down social media accounts by username across social networks
sections.content: A command-line tool that searches for a username across hundreds of social networks. It leads today's list by daily gains; its README documents a focused CLI workflow across 400+ networks with export options.
sections.why_notable: It leads today's list by daily gains, and its README documents a focused CLI workflow across 400+ networks with export options.
sections.unique_caveat: A username match is a search result to investigate, not proof that accounts belong to the same real-world person.

enrichment.architecture_summary: A Python command-line search tool that checks candidate usernames against a maintained collection of social-network sites.
enrichment.workflow: Install the CLI, supply one or more usernames, optionally select sites or output format, and review the resulting account-presence report.
enrichment.design_pattern: A single CLI orchestrates many site-specific checks and writes evidence to portable output files.

sections.title: meta/astryx
sections.description: An open source design system that's fully customizable and agent ready
sections.content: Meta's open-source design system for customizable React interfaces and AI-assisted development. Its README describes 150+ accessible components, theming, and CLI tooling designed for developers and agents.
sections.why_notable: It is the day's second-largest star-gain signal; its README describes 150+ accessible components, theming, and a CLI designed for both developers and agents.
sections.unique_caveat: The current README labels the project as in beta.

enrichment.architecture_summary: A React 19+ design system built on StyleX, organized into published core and CLI packages with reusable components, themes, and tooling.
core_components: typed React components and pre-built CSS
CLI for component documentation, templates, scaffolding, themes, and codemods
enrichment.workflow: Install the core package and CLI, use documented components and templates, adjust theme variables, and use CLI commands to discover or scaffold project pieces.
enrichment.design_pattern: Open composable internals with a swizzle/eject path, documented conventions, and a shared human-and-agent API; no styling-library adoption is required by the README's stated workflow.

sections.title: milind-soni/OpenMausBot
sections.description: Open-source Grok Bot alternative with a virtual machine that bots can use
sections.content: An open-source Grok Bot alternative described as including a virtual machine that bots can use.
sections.why_notable: It places third by daily gains, illustrating demand for alternative bot runtimes; the repository's own description is the main available evidence for its design.
sections.unique_caveat: The description is brief and does not independently substantiate the virtual-machine architecture.

sections.title: anthropics/skills
sections.content: Anthropic's collection of reusable Claude skills, each packaged as a folder of instructions, scripts, and resources for specialized tasks.
sections.why_notable: The repository presents skills as self-contained instruction, script, and resource folders loaded for specialized tasks, a portable pattern for agent workflows.
sections.unique_caveat: The README frames the included implementations as demonstration and educational material.

enrichment.architecture_summary: Skills are modular folders containing instruction files, scripts, and supporting resources; Claude loads them dynamically for specialized tasks.
enrichment.workflow: Select or create a self-contained skill folder, then use it in Claude.ai, Claude Code, or through the Claude API integrations described in the README.
enrichment.design_pattern: Small, reusable task modules that encode repeatable procedures and can carry task-specific assets alongside instructions.

sections.title: vercel-labs/agent-browser
sections.description: Browser automation CLI for AI agents
sections.content: A Rust CLI for agents to inspect pages as compact accessibility snapshots, act on element references, and verify outcomes step by step.
sections.why_notable: Its accessibility-tree snapshots and element references make browser work a compact, verifiable command loop.
sections.unique_caveat: Actions can fail when targets are hidden, disabled, outside the viewport, or covered; the README instructs callers to refresh state and retry.

enrichment.architecture_summary: A native Rust command-line client sends commands to a background daemon that controls a browser over Chrome DevTools Protocol; sessions use separate daemons and browsers.
core_components: compact accessibility snapshots with element references
enrichment.workflow: Open a page, request an interactive snapshot, act on an element reference, and inspect the resulting URL or fresh page snapshot; the browser persists between commands.
enrichment.design_pattern: A short observe-act-verify shell loop with explicit page state, rather than returning success without checking the browser result.

sections.title: google-deepmind/mujoco
sections.description: Multi-Joint dynamics with Contact. A general purpose physics simulator.
sections.content: A general-purpose physics simulator for multi-joint dynamics with contact, representing robotics and simulation in today's trending set.
sections.why_notable: It is a research and robotics counterpoint to the agent-heavy leaders, showing sustained interest in simulation infrastructure.

sections.title: anthropics/claude-quickstarts
sections.description: A collection of projects designed to help developers quickly get started with building deployable applications using the Claude API
sections.content: A collection of starter projects for building deployable applications with the Claude API.
sections.why_notable: Its practical application templates complement skills and agent tooling with concrete starting points for API-powered products.
sections.unique_caveat: These are starting-point projects; the repository description does not establish production readiness for a given use.

sections.title: ZhuLinsen/daily_stock_analysis
sections.description: LLM-powered multi-market stock-analysis system with multi-source market data, real-time news, a decision dashboard, and automated notifications.
sections.content: An LLM-driven stock-analysis application that combines multi-source market data and news with a dashboard and scheduled notifications.
sections.why_notable: It brings the agent trend into a vertical application, combining market-data collection and analysis with a dashboard and scheduled delivery.

sections.title: ruvnet/RuView
sections.description: Turns commodity Wi-Fi signals into spatial intelligence, vital-sign monitoring, and presence detection without video.
sections.content: A Wi-Fi sensing platform using channel-state information from low-cost ESP32 sensors to infer movement and breathing without cameras.
sections.why_notable: Its README describes using Wi-Fi channel-state information from low-cost ESP32 sensors to infer movement and breathing, a distinctive edge-sensing direction.
sections.unique_caveat: The README's sensing workflow relies on channel-state information capture with low-cost ESP32 sensors; it is not simply a software-only setup using any router.

enrichment.architecture_summary: A Wi-Fi sensing platform captures channel-state information using low-cost ESP32 sensors and processes signal changes into spatial and vital-sign estimates.
enrichment.workflow: Capture CSI, prepare or train a model, load the model for inference, and connect the resulting sensing data to supported tools such as Home Assistant.
enrichment.design_pattern: An edge-sensor plus signal-processing pipeline that uses radio perturbations rather than cameras or wearables as its sensing input.

sections.title: garrytan/gbrain
sections.content: An opinionated agent-brain project for OpenClaw and Hermes, representing persistent context and personalization in the agent tooling cluster.
sections.why_notable: It represents the agent-memory/personalization layer, complementing the skills, browser, and API-building projects higher in the list.
sections.unique_caveat: Its description calls it opinionated; behavior and compatibility depend on the specific agent setup.

sections.title: homeassistant-ai/ha-mcp
sections.description: Configure and automate Home Assistant with Claude, ChatGPT, and other AI assistants.
sections.content: An MCP integration for configuring and automating Home Assistant from AI assistants.
sections.why_notable: It is a smaller but concrete example of model-context tooling connecting assistants to an existing home-automation platform.

sections.title: Trending Technologies and Themes
sections.content: Agent workflows and infrastructure appear across anthropics/skills, anthropics/claude-quickstarts, garrytan/gbrain, vercel-labs/agent-browser, and milind-soni/OpenMausBot. Astryx brings a substantial React design system to agent-oriented frontend work. Sherlock leads the non-agent signal with username search across social networks. MuJoCo and RuView represent simulation and radio sensing; daily_stock_analysis and ha-mcp are vertical AI integrations. Languages: Python 5, TypeScript 3, Rust 2, C++ 1.

sections.title: Takeaway
sections.content: Today's signal is not just “more AI”: developers are gravitating toward agent-ready interfaces and capabilities that connect models to browsers, APIs, persistent context, and real-world services. At the same time, Sherlock's lead and attention to simulation and Wi-Fi sensing show that broad developer utility and physical-world computing still compete strongly for stars.

sections.title: Sources and Method
sections.content: Primary source: https://github.com/trending?since=daily, captured 2026-11-09 17:43 UTC. Corroboration: GitHub REST repository and default-branch commit endpoints, plus GitHub Search API for repositories created 2026-11-07 through 2026-11-09 and pushed since 2026-11-07. Daily gains and total stars use the values displayed on the captured daily Trending view; entries are ordered by daily star gains. Search-only noise was not promoted. No prior-window evidence was used, so no Notable Shifts section is claimed.
